decisions.quote: This study presents a three-year replication and extension of Maurer’s (2013) evaluation of a classroom activity to reduce prejudice and discrimination.
decisions.reason: The paper collects new classroom data over three years in six course sections to re-test Maurer's (2013) empirical evaluation of the BSDS classroom activity.

decisions.quote:
Results differed
                    significantly from those reported by Maurer (2013), and suggested that all three methods tested were equally
                    effective in reducing prejudice and discrimination and that such changes were lasting.
decisions.reason: Maurer's (2013) central finding was a greater positive shift in BSDS attitudes in the activity condition relative to lecture-only control. Here, the Time x Condition interaction was nonsignificant (failing to support Hypothesis 2a/2b), and the authors explicitly conclude that their results differed significantly from and diverged from Maurer (2013). The partial support mentioned in the discussion pertains to Hypothesis 3 (the new atheist target-group extension), not to Maurer (2013).
